newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt may use more confidence votes on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt may use more confidence votes on budget.

text.p: The Italian cabinet has decided to call more confidence votes if necessary to get the 1997 budget through parliament, civil service minister Franco Bassanini said on Tuesday.

He said the decision applied to both the Senate (upper house), where votes on outstanding articles of the bill are still pending, and in the lower Chamber of Deputies, where the package must return for a final reading.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government won three confidence votes in the Senate on Monday which it had called to sweep aside a welter of opposition amendments blocking passage of the 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) package.
Opposition senators boycotted the votes and a subsequent ballot on the budget bill, which the government won 164-0.
Bassanini said opposition amendments to the so-called financial law, part of the budget package, could hold up its passage by a Senate deadline of December 19.

"We have authority to call a confidence vote on article two of the financial law because it's the one with the most opposition amendments but the decision still has to be taken," Bassanini said. Asked if the government could seek a confidence vote in the Chamber, where it hopes the package will be approved by December 23, Bassanini replied "Yes".
